Create a gig plot specification

gig.Rd

gig() starts a plot of a hierarchical or grouped time series. It holds the data, the default aesthetic mapping and, optionally, the aggregation structure. Components are then added with +:

Usage

gig(data, mapping = gig_aes(), structure = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame. For geom_features(), one row per series containing the key columns and numeric feature columns. For geom_stl(), a table of STL components. For geom_sunburst(), any table containing the key columns.

mapping

A gig_aes() mapping. Layers may override it.

structure

Optional aggregation structure. Either a bare expression such as (State / Region) * Purpose, a string such as "(State/Region)*Purpose", or a hierarchy() object. Adding + hierarchy(...) afterwards overrides it.

Value

An object of class gig.

Details

  • one geom_*() layer, geom_features(), geom_stl() or geom_sunburst();

  • a hierarchy() specification, if it was not supplied through structure;

  • a gig_aes() mapping, which is merged into the plot mapping.

The plot is drawn when it is printed. Use gig_build() to obtain the underlying htmlwidget, for example to save it with htmlwidgets::saveWidget().

See also

gig_aes(), hierarchy(), gig_build()

Examples

library(fabletools)
library(feasts)

tas_tourism <- aus_tourism[aus_tourism$State == "Tasmania", ]
tas_features <- tas_tourism |>
  aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips)) |>
  features(Trips, feat_stl)

gig(tas_features,
    gig_aes(x = trend_strength, y = seasonal_strength_year),
    structure = (State / Region) * Purpose) +
  geom_features()
